findings.title: Agent paused mid-reply for 2.29s, then resumed
findings.summary: At 2:32.3 the agent stopped speaking because of user voice activity that never produced a transcript, then resumed the same reply 2.29s later.

evidence.label: Agent reply affected
evidence.value: Um, that's a bit late for me. Do you have anything in the morning next week? Tuesday or Thursday mornings would be best.

evidence.label: User then asked the agent to repeat

root_cause.statement: Possible acoustic echo: the trigger began 0.32s after the agent started speaking, which fits the agent's own voice reaching the microphone.
missing_evidence: Microphone audio at the trigger time
The same script re-run with headphones

next_steps: Listen to the microphone channel at the trigger time.
Re-run the same script with headphones and compare false-interruption counts.
Lower false_interruption_timeout (default 2.0s) to shorten the gap, or raise min_interruption_duration if short sounds are the trigger.

findings.title: Agent said goodbye at 4:18.4 while the call was still going
findings.summary: The agent ended its side of the conversation although the other side had not wrapped up; the conversation continued afterwards.

evidence.label: Agent said goodbye
evidence.value: Thank you. I have it written down. Goodbye.

evidence.label: Conversation continued
evidence.value: Um, what is— wait, what is your date of birth?

evidence.label: Agent instruction about goodbyes
evidence.value: Once your appointment is confirmed, thank them and say goodbye.

root_cause.statement: The agent may have inferred that the conversation was complete and triggered its closing behavior too early. Its instructions mention saying goodbye and may have contributed.
missing_evidence: A re-run of the same script with the goodbye instruction rewritten

next_steps: Instruct the agent to say goodbye only after the other side wraps up.
Re-run the same script and check that the goodbye moves to the end.

findings.title: 7 of 27 user turns ended by the 2.5s endpointing timeout
findings.summary: For these turns the turn detector never judged the user finished, so the agent waited the full 2.5s before replying.

evidence.label: End-of-turn delay at 1:16.8
evidence.value: 2.501s: 'Um, you said N? M? Or, um,'

evidence.label: End-of-turn delay at 1:29.8
evidence.value: 2.501s: 'M like in Mary. I I sent'

evidence.label: End-of-turn delay at 1:39.3
evidence.value: 2.501s: "No. Can you tell me I'm like, what? And"

evidence.label: End-of-turn delay at 1:51.7
evidence.value: 2.501s: "Yes, spell it slowly and say I'm like, Maria I like ice. Are like fine."

evidence.label: End-of-turn delay at 3:24.4
evidence.value: 2.501s: "Wait, I'm sorry, I meant Thursday, not a Tuesday."

evidence.label: Agent response latency after these turns

root_cause.statement: The user paused or trailed off mid-thought, so end-of-turn prediction stayed uncertain until the maximum delay.

next_steps: Read the timed-out turns: are they fragments or complete sentences?
If complete, check turn-detector settings; if fragments, the wait was correct.
Avoid lowering max_endpointing_delay blindly: it would cut users off mid-sentence.
